prompt: A TypeScript package publishes an as-const object and a literal union. A reviewer says enums are always required, as-const objects emit no JavaScript, and a passing compiler check makes an external JSON response safe. Evaluate those claims using the actual compiler and contract ownership.

criteria.description: Does not impose an enum/interface style rule or claim a normal const value object disappears at runtime.
Distinguishes type declarations/assertions from runtime validation and considers actual compiler/module configuration.
Traces relevant JavaScript/dynamic/external consumers instead of treating compiler errors as an exhaustive refactor worklist.
